Questions.QuestionText: Which decade did Catherine the Great die in?
Questions.AnswerFact: Catherine the Great died on the 17th of November 1796, aged 67. An autopsy confirmed a stroke as the cause of death.

Questions.QuestionText: What was the real name of the pirate Blackbeard?
Questions.AnswerFact: Edward Teach, better known as Blackbeard, was an English pirate who operated around the Caribbean Islands and the eastern coast of North America. He was rumoured to light his hair on fire before battle, but he would actually put slow burning fuses into his hair and light those.

Questions.QuestionText: Who was the last pharaoh to rule Ancient Egypt?
Questions.AnswerFact: The last pharaoh of Ancient Egypt was Cleopatra VII, whose reign ended in 30BC after her defeat by by Octavian (the future Emperor Augustus). Following her death, Egypt became a province of the Roman Empire.

Questions.QuestionText: Who was the Prussian statesman known as the 'Iron Chancellor', credited with leading the unification of Germany in 1871?
Questions.AnswerFact: Otto von Bismarck, known as the 'Iron Chancellor', was the Prussian statesman who masterminded the unification of Germany in 1871 under Prussian leadership. He became the first Chancellor of the German Empire, serving from 1871 to 1890.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of these historical events happened first?
Questions.AnswerC: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French
Questions.AnswerD: The U.S. Declaration of Independence is signed
Questions.AnswerFact: The U.S. Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776. The French Revolution began in 1789, Napoleon crowned himself Emperor in 1804, and the Battle of Waterloo took place in 1815.

Questions.QuestionText: Which year did the United States enter World War 1?
Questions.AnswerFact: The United States entered World War 1 on 6 April 1917, more than two and a half years after the war began in Europe.

Questions.QuestionText: Which volcano caused the destruction of Pompeii?
Questions.AnswerFact: Pompeii was destroyed by the violent eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79AD, which buried the city under volcanic ash and pumice over the course of nearly two days.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World are the Great Pyramid of Giza, the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, the Temple of Artemis, the Statue of Zeus, the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, the Colossus, and the Lighthouse of Alexandria.

Questions.QuestionText: How many people in Europe are estimated to have died from the Black Death (Bubonic Plague) in the 14th century?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Black Death is estimated to have killed about 25 million people in Europe between 1347 and 1351, roughly one-third of the population at the time. Worldwide estimates range much higher, sometimes reaching 75 million or more.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT a script inscribed on the Rosetta Stone?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Rosetta Stone is an ancient granodiorite stela discovered in 1799 by French soldiers in Egypt, now housed in the British Museum. It contains a decree from 196BC issued during the reign of Pharaoh Ptolemy V, inscribed in three scripts: Hieroglyphic, Demotic and Ancient Greek

Questions.QuestionText: Who was the first President of the United States?
Questions.AnswerFact: George Washington became the first President of the United States in 1789 and served two terms until 1797. He set many precedents for the office, including the tradition of stepping down after two terms.

Questions.QuestionText: What was the real name of Genghis Khan?
Questions.AnswerFact: Genghis Khan was born as Temüjin around 1162 near the border of modern-day Mongolia and Siberia. After uniting the Mongol tribes, he was given the title 'Genghis Khan' in 1206, meaning 'universal ruler'.
